metadata.title: Teaching and Learning International Survey (TALIS) 2018 Conceptual Framework (EN)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The document specifies TALIS 2018’s sampling and weighting approach for producing population-representative estimates. The main survey targets approximately 200 schools per country and 20 teachers per school (nominal international sample size 4,000 teachers), with schools sampled with probability proportional to size and teachers sampled within schools. It states that survey weights are computed to account for the sample design and differences in participation, and that applying survey weights is essential for analyses and for estimating sampling error. The framework does not name specific weight variables (e.g., TOTWGT/W_FSTUWT) or replicate-weight methods, so analysts should consult the TALIS 2018 technical documentation/user guide for the exact weight and variance-estimation variables to use.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This is a conceptual framework and survey-design document rather than an empirical analysis paper. It does not report any plausible-value generation or PV-based achievement outcomes; TALIS 2018 is based on teacher and principal questionnaire responses and the framework focuses on themes, indicators, and survey operations. Missing-data handling strategies (e.g., imputation or deletion rules) are not specified because the document is intended to guide instrument development and survey implementation, not to analyze a dataset with a documented missing-data protocol.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The framework defines the TALIS 2018 target populations and exclusions rather than reporting an analytic dataset. Core target population is lower secondary (ISCED 2) teachers and their school principals; international options include ISCED 1 and ISCED 3 teachers/principals and a school-level link to PISA 2018 (teachers eligible to teach 15-year-olds in PISA-participating schools). It specifies that schools exclusively for adult education and schools exclusively for students with special needs are out of scope, and that substitute/emergency teachers are excluded. It also sets participation requirements (minimum 75% school response after replacement, with a minimum 50% teacher response within participating schools; and minimum 75% teacher participation per country) and notes an upper limit of 5% teacher exclusion from the ISCED 2 survey population for consistency with prior cycles.

data.outcome_summary: This document is a TALIS 2018 conceptual framework and survey-design guide, not an empirical study estimating effects with machine learning. It defines TALIS as an international large-scale survey of teachers, school leaders, and their learning environments, administered primarily in lower secondary (ISCED 2) with optional modules for ISCED 1 and ISCED 3 and an optional TALIS–PISA link. The framework specifies the thematic structure (teacher instructional and professional practices; teacher education/initial preparation; feedback and development; self-efficacy; job satisfaction/motivation; school leadership and climate; human resource and stakeholder relations; innovation; equity and diversity) and explains how indicators support cross-country and trend analyses. For survey operations, it outlines sampling (probability proportional to size for schools; teachers within schools), target sample sizes (about 200 schools per country and 20 teachers per school; nominal 4,000 teachers), response-rate requirements, and the need for survey weights to produce representative estimates. It also emphasizes measurement invariance as a prerequisite for valid comparisons across countries and over time.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is sparse by design because the source is a conceptual framework/survey operations document rather than an empirical analysis paper. It does not provide an analytic sample with country-level Ns, does not specify PVs or missing-data handling procedures for an outcome model, and does not train or evaluate any ML algorithms. Consequently, fields such as main_findings, confounders, and ML techniques are intentionally empty.
